item.title: [45] Task force report on CBP misconduct & corruption
item.description: The final report of an independent task force on misconduct and corruption in U.S. Customs and Border Protection, including the Border Patrol. (Published 3/15/16) | 58 pages | Source: Tucson Sentinel

item.title: [45] Ruling: Tucson city elections are unconstititional
item.description: Sending the case back to a lower court, a panel of federal judges has ruled that Tucson's "odd" system of electing its City Council violates the principle of "one person, one vote." The 9th Circuit released the 2-1 decision Tuesday. (Published 11/10/15) | 25 pages | Source: Tucson Sentinel

item.title: [45] Ruling dismissing GOP election suit
item.description: A Superior Court judge ruled Monday against a request by a pair of Republican candidates who sought to be declared the winners of last month's Tucson election. Kelly Lawton and Margaret Burkholder won their East Side wards, but lost in landslides in the total vote count. (Published 12/7/15) Related: https://www.tucsonsentinel.com/local/report/120715_council_suit | 3 pages | Source: Tucson Sentinel

item.title: [45] Ruling: 'Return to Mexico' policy blocked by judge
item.description: A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration's "Migrant Protection Protocols" that would return asylum seekers to Mexico, ruling that the change violated the law. (Published 4/8/19) | 27 pages | Source: Tucson Sentinel

item.title: [45] Ruling: Arpaio ordered to halt racial profiling
item.description: Maricopa County Sheriff Joe Arpaio violated the civil rights of Latinos who were detained during immigration sweeps, a federal judge ruled Friday. The 142-page decision came in a case that alleged Arpaio and his deputies relied on race in determining who to target for immigration enforcement. (Published 5/24/13) | 142 pages | Source: Tucson Sentinel

item.title: [45] Ruling: Family can sue BP agent in 2012 shooting death of Mexican boy
item.description: A federal judge ruled Thursday that a civil rights lawsuit can proceed against a Border Patrol agent who shot and killed a 16-year-old boy through the border fence in Nogales in 2012. Agent Lonnie Swartz is being sued by the family of Jose Antonio Elena Rodriguez, who was shot approximately 10 times. (Published 7/10/15) Related: https://www.tucsonsentinel.com/local/report/070915_bp_shootingsuit | 21 pages | Source: Tucson Sentinel

item.title: [45] Indictment of BP Agent Lonnie Swartz
item.description: U.S. Border Patrol Agent Lonnie Swartz has been indicted for second-degree murder in the shooting of 16-year Jose Antonio Elena Rodriguez through the border fence in Nogales during an Oct. 10, 2012, incident. (Published 9/24/15) | 1 pages | Source: Tucson Sentinel

item.title: [45] Ruling: Supreme Court upholds Arizona redistricting
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled 5-4 on Monday that Arizona's nonpartisan redistricting process is constitutional. (Published 6/29/15) | 81 pages | Source: Tucson Sentinel

item.title: [45] 5th Circuit ruling on DACA injunction
item.description: A federal appeals court rejected Tuesday the Obama administration's request to remove an injunction that has stalled two programs intended to offer protection for deportation as well as work permits to million of immigrants in the United States without authorization. (Published 5/26/15) | 68 pages | Source: Tucson Sentinel

item.title: [45] Justice seeks stay in DACA/DAPA case
item.description: Arguing that the government will be “irreparably harmed” by an court order that keeps federal officials from implementing two deferred action programs for immigrants, Department of Justice lawyers requested Monday that the order be stayed until the case can be appealed. (Published 2/23/15) Related: https://www.tucsonsentinel.com/local/report/022315_stay_texas_injunction | 24 pages | Source: Tucson Sentinel

item.title: [45] Judge's DAPA/DACA opinion: Texas v United States
item.description: A U.S. District Court judge issued a temporary injunction late Monday night, ordering the Department of Homeland Security to halt expansions to the deferred action program. DAPA and DACA were announced in November by President Obama. (Published 2/17/15) Related: https://www.tucsonsentinel.com/local/news/021615_dapa-daca | 89 pages | Source: Tucson Sentinel
